phase_1_foundation.description: Initial game implementation with core mechanics

key_achievements: Dynamic grid scaling for responsive design
Standalone level editor (later removed in Phase 6)

phase_5b_maintenance.description: Code quality, dependency updates, and maintenance

phase_6_refactor.description: Major architectural refactor: Python MILP solver, browser as checker-only
key_achievements: Replaced JavaScript solver with Python MILP solver (PuLP + CBC)
Browser code reduced to pure checker (no solver, no generator)
Fixed level selector crash when switching map sizes
Updated all documentation to reflect new architecture

map_generation.description: AI struggled significantly with puzzle generation algorithms, ultimately resolved by switching from JavaScript to Python MILP
problems: Minimizing instead of maximizing penned area
Time-limited solvers produced poor quality maps
JavaScript fundamentally wrong tool for MILP optimization
map_generation.solution: Replaced entire JS solver with Python MILP solver (PuLP + CBC), making browser checker-only

testing_complexity.description: Building comprehensive test infrastructure was challenging
testing_complexity.solution: Proper Jest setup with JSDOM and skipped performance tests

architecture_drift.description: Code organization needed periodic cleanup, culminating in major refactor
problems: Test utilities mixed with production code
Solver code in browser that belonged in build pipeline
architecture_drift.solution: Major refactor separating browser (checker) from build pipeline (solver), extracted shared utilities

what_worked_well: Performing large-scale refactors with clear instructions
what_struggled: Catching subtle logic bugs (maximize vs minimize)
Maintaining separation of concerns across PRs
Choosing the right technology for specialized problems
lessons_learned: AI excels at well-defined, localized tasks
Complex algorithms need human oversight and verification
Documentation is critical for AI to maintain consistency
Iterative refinement works better than big-bang changes
Testing helps catch AI mistakes early
Technology choice (which language/tool to use) remains a human judgment
AI can execute major refactors effectively once humans define the target architecture
